title: Check the pinned Git tree before treating a sparse-checkout file as missing
applies_when: A source review or native import preflight cannot find contribution instructions, a companion Python package, or another tracked file in a sparse checkout.
lesson: Inspect git sparse-checkout list and git ls-tree at the exact commit, then read the existing blob with git show. Files excluded from the working tree are not absent from the repository. This can avoid recreating a compatibility shim or ignoring review guidance. Explicitly select and hash an existing same-source companion package when testing it; record its module origin separately from installed distribution metadata. The existing raw-Git source bundler can export a committed path that is absent from a sparse working tree without changing its sparse patterns or materializing that source checkout.
avoid_when: A missing object in a partial clone, Git submodule, generated build output, or genuinely absent pinned-tree path needs different handling. The bundler does not silently fetch missing objects. Finding source does not prove installed dependencies, binary compatibility, native execution or PR readiness. Do not alter another task's sparse patterns or shared installation to make a diagnostic pass. Source availability and a native Git fixture do not establish Scout recall, saved tokens or knowledge benefit.

evidence.note: Git documents that sparse checkout materializes only a subset of tracked files; list reports selected directories or patterns. Its absence from the working tree is not a missing-tree-path result. Mechanism, not a performance claim.

The pinned raw Git blob contains the provider-discovery shim even when the companion directory is excluded by local sparse patterns. The blob was independently read from existing local Git objects; this is source-location evidence, not a FlashInfer import, GPU, ABI or complete native qualification.
